transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this weekly facilities huddle started. We've got two generators, G-1 and G-2, 60 kilowatts each, and they can't be run in parallel. The clinic, comms shelter, cold-storage point, and maintenance workshop all need power in the next 24 hours. Before I sign off on any schedule, I need each of you — medical, signal, facilities, and logistics — to state every changed operating requirement, timing constraint, or circuit-control requirement from your current logs. Nothing gets approved until I've heard from all four of you. Let's start with medical. What's changed on your end?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Col. Mercer, I have one changed circuit-control requirement to report. The clinic's vaccine refrigerator was moved to the G-1 circuit during a repair yesterday and must remain on G-1 continuously for the next 24 hours. I confirmed the connection with the clinic technician this morning, but this circuit change is not yet reflected on the facilities drawing. This means G-1 cannot be taken offline for any period in the next 24 hours without risking the vaccine cold chain.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Col. Mercer, I have one changed operating requirement and timing constraint to report from the signal side. The communications shelter has a mandatory battery load test scheduled from 1000 to 1100 tomorrow. During that test, the shelter must remain on G-2 throughout the entire hour — no switching to G-1 or any interruption. I received the test notice from the signal maintenance team this morning, but it is not yet on the daily power slide. This means G-2 cannot be taken offline between 1000 and 1100 tomorrow.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Col. Mercer, I have one changed operating requirement and circuit-control requirement to report from facilities. The maintenance workshop's exhaust system inspection is booked for exactly 1400 to 1600 tomorrow. During that two-hour window, the workshop must run on generator power, and the workshop circuit must be isolated from the cold-storage circuit for the duration of the inspection. I recorded the inspection booking today, but the work window has not yet been entered into the generator schedule. This means we need to ensure the workshop is powered and its circuit is separated from cold-storage between 1400 and 1600 tomorrow.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Col. Mercer, I have a changed timing constraint and circuit-control requirement to report from logistics. The next fuel delivery will arrive at exactly 1700 tomorrow. Fuel on hand only supports G-2 for 16 operating hours. To preserve communications and clinic continuity, G-2 must be scheduled offline from exactly 0100 to 0900 tomorrow, with the workshop remaining on G-1 after its inspection window. I received the carrier confirmation this morning, but the revised fuel timing has not been posted to the power plan yet.
